about: Brand-neutral catalogue of module/technique patterns, not a claim that every consuming client implements them. Resolve aliases and category before adding a module. Each entry carries concrete bypass_tips, prerequisites, flag_triggers and target-specific validation scenarios. Risk is an engineering heuristic, not server acceptance. Reference paths are relative to this catalogue; anticheat-bypass.md is the single detailed detector/action-validation reference. General state, navigation and protocol contracts are in the main skill.

primitives: triangular reactionMs (mid-biased, avg of two uniforms)
humanization.reaction_gate: arms a randomized delay on the rising edge of a stimulus; true only once it elapses, resets when the stimulus goes away — one fresh reaction per appearance

mouse_gcd.formula: f = sens*0.6 + 0.2; deg_per_count = f^3 * 1.2 (mirrors vanilla sensitivity math exactly)
rules: snap the wire rotation to the grid anchored on last-sent: base + round((target-base)/gcd)*gcd
if a step rounds to 0 but target >=1 count away, take sign(delta)*gcd so it never stalls
carry the sub-count remainder across ticks (a real mouse accumulates)
advance eased aim on real dt (sub-tick); snap only the value that leaves on a packet
Emit every camera and server-path contributor through a shared whole-mouse-count applier with carried remainder; avoid a second quantizer or independent fractional click jitter.

eased_rotator: AR(1) hand drift driftYaw=driftYaw*0.92+jitter(0.04) (pitch 0.03), amplitude ~0.1deg so a held aim is never frozen
ease-out settle with a firm floor clamp(max(|dYaw|,|dPitch|)/12,0.34,1)

per-tick pace = logNormal(sigma=0.14, clamp 0.72..1.6): a right-skewed median-1 multiplier (exp(N(0,0.14))), NOT the old symmetric uniform x[0.85,1.15] band — this is an optional distribution to compare with a measured baseline, not proof of human origin
a hair of positional jitter while turning: +jitter(0.12) yaw / jitter(0.08) pitch above 1.5deg of remaining delta
overshoot min(|d|*0.12,6) over 25deg turns, decays x0.55/tick (zeroed under 0.4), ~500ms cooldown
Whole-count emission on camera and server paths; apply final combined speed/acceleration and disabled-axis constraints after feed-forward and noise.

reset() on disengage (active=false, overshoot/drift/ticks cleared) so the next engagement eases in fresh instead of continuing mid-swing; the aim CONTROLLER additionally resets reaction delay + ease-in + overshoot on a target switch
humanization.calibration_scope: Controller composition and numeric coefficients are examples to validate against actual input/serialization and a relevant baseline; no distribution or grid match proves human origin or server acceptance.
humanization.elapsed_time_contract: Convert fixed-cadence filters to alpha=1-exp(-dt/tau). For stationary AR noise use a=exp(-dt/tau) and innovation sigma*sqrt(1-a*a). Fixed per-tick examples must not be copied as per-render-frame coefficients; drop stall catch-up and bound the final combined output.

rotation_ownership.problem: last-writer-wins -> two placement modules flicker the rotation; one module's release cancels another's in-progress hold
rotation_ownership.solution: ControlClaim{owner, priority, lastRefresh}; aim(yaw,pitch,dist,token,correctMovement); a live owner (refreshed <~120ms) keeps it unless the newcomer is strictly higher priority; a stale claim is free to take; release(token) is a no-op unless token holds it; on release ease the server rotation back to the camera (no snap)
rotation_ownership.two_packet_paths: the move packet carries one rotation but a use-item/interact packet carries its OWN; feed the silent rotation into the use path for that one interaction (a useWithSilent flag) or throws/places fire where the camera points
movement_correction: Proper: re-pick WASD against the server yaw, snap to nearest of 8 dirs, sprint only when forward of it
Slow: keep real keys, kill sprint past 45deg off-facing
rotation_ownership.action_result: Return applied/refused explicitly; delayed uses recheck current ownership and held-item prerequisites before acting. Camera, movement, attack, use and hotbar controls need distinct ownership boundaries.

prediction_sim.recipe: AABB from start pos+vel; loop ticks applying real accel/drag; per-axis collision sweep (Shapes.collide Y then X then Z vs swept block shapes); read-only; cap the tick budget; act on where things WILL be — the resulting packet is legal so the server can't object
prediction_sim.fall: vy=(vy-0.08)*0.98, horizontal air drag 0.91 only on an uncollided axis, ~70 tick cap -> {lands,voided,landX,landZ,drop,water}; simulates the real arc so knockback/momentum throws are caught and the true landing column feeds placement
prediction_sim.mace_impact: a smash does most damage on the last airborne tick: hold the attack while falling, release only when stepping one fall move ahead collides; a >5 drop smashes immediately to avoid clipping the ground
prediction_sim.projectile: per-type constants (ender pearl: gravity 0.03, drag 0.99, throw 1.5); predict an enemy projectile's landing from its pos+vel, OR brute-force your launch pitch over a range, simulate each, keep the nearest-landing, add inherited horizontal velocity, throw only if miss < tolerance

baseline: reaction (triangular, new target) + shorter reacquire (target back from behind cover) delays
multi-octave sinusoidal shake applied as per-frame delta
upgrades: Target-rate feed-forward with alpha=1-exp(-dt/tau); reset target samples on identity changes/teleports/gaps, keep camera momentum separate, and bound the final combined output instead of only the base correction.
adaptive speed scale=clamp(|dYaw|/20,0.35,1.5), softer when on-target
per-target randomized gains x0.8-1.2 + per-tick lognormal speed with point-blank slowdown

clicks: fatigue+bursts: top of range ~1.5s then 0.15+0.75*e^(-(t-1.5)/12), recovery between fights
styles: Jitter/Butterfly/Drag all averaging to CPS
Click Assist amplifies real clicks only
stand down while an aura drives the attack
Every primary/assist/second click rechecks current input, focus, menu, target, charge and ownership gates; cancel stale work on disable or session replacement.
Use explicit monotonic-clock units, preserve configured CPS meaning and avoid catch-up bursts after stalls; double-click rhythms are optional, not universal requirements.
packets: Owner-aware rule slots with connection/world generations and stale-producer cancellation.
Bound held age/count independently of optional Auto Send; queue budgets do not guarantee server acceptance.
Classify movement plus version-specific tick-end batches; define ordered pass, flush-before-pass and effective control handling even behind a held incoming head.
Correction/disconnect/configuration/respawn barriers need explicit ordered drain or semantic discard; never replay on a replacement connection/world.

movement_physics.about: Every movement module rides vanilla physics; reproduce the integration exactly (and per engine version) because a prediction anticheat runs the same replay. Per-tick order: apply input accel -> move with per-axis collision sweep (Y then X then Z, same as the prediction sims) -> apply drag/friction for next tick -> gravity.

constants.horizontal_friction: vx,vz *= friction next tick; friction = onGround ? blockSlipperiness*0.91 : 0.91. Default slipperiness 0.6 -> ground 0.546, air 0.91. Slipperiness: ice/packed-ice 0.98, blue-ice 0.989, slime 0.8
constants.acceleration: ground = moveSpeed * (0.21600002 / friction^3); air = flat ~0.02. moveSpeed = walk attribute base 0.1 * 1.3 while sprinting (sprint is a transient +30% attribute modifier, not a velocity hack)
constants.jump: vy = 0.42 (+0.1*(JumpBoost+1)); a sprint-jump adds a one-off horizontal 0.2 along facing yaw (the biggest legal ground-speed burst, the honest basis for Bhop)
constants.use_item_slowdown: while isUsingItem() and not riding, forward/strafe INPUT is scaled by 0.2 before acceleration; sneak scales input by 0.3 (input multipliers, not speed caps)

modules.step: Use scoped transient modifiers rather than overwriting a base, but verify that the server actually authorizes the same height before relying on it.
modules.speed_bhop: Use the actual authorized sprint-jump launch and subsequent input/friction; unsupported velocity remains invalid even if its magnitude resembles a normal jump.
modules.strafe_air_accel: rewrite air input toward the move vector each tick, respecting the 0.02 air-accel cap; never add velocity the input couldn't
modules.longjump: slipperiness-aware launch, but horizontal still decays by the block friction each tick and the impulse must be one a jump could legally produce
modules.noslow: Skipping the use-item multiplier can disagree with server-authoritative movement. Keep unrelated modifiers intact but validate the changed trajectory; no universal safe mode is implied.
modules.keepsprint_omnisprint: Distinguish entry from continuation. Authorized modern sprint flight can retain forward+strafe and altitude input after a brief vanilla sprint press. Do not repeatedly force isSprinting after cancellation; coordinate owners and release for unsafe/non-forward input. A vanilla field alone does not establish server acceptance.
modules.velocity: scale deltaMovement after the server applies KB, with precision jitter so the result is never a clean fraction of the push (see modules.Velocity)
modules.authorized_flight: Read server flying speed and actual version physics; checked 26.2/26.3 sprint flight doubles horizontal input acceleration. Predict diagonal boosted input, full-body braking and combined vertical clearance. Prevent automated ascent pulses from accumulating the manual flight-double-tap timer while the bot owns active authorized flight.

movement_physics.universal_rule: Reproduce final input and authoritative state in the supported version; local attribute/ability changes, plausible magnitudes or stochastic variation do not establish server acceptance.

targeting.about: Combat modules share one TargetSetting so target policy is set once and obeyed everywhere (who to aim at, who to never touch).
targeting.target_setting: bundles entity TYPES (Players/Mobs/Animals, picked with popout tabs) with FILTERS (ignore invisible / naked / behind-walls / friends / teammates / bots) and an optional Max Distance. test(e) = not the local player AND matches: right type and enabled, within range, line-of-sight (clip eye->eye or eye->body-centre, cached per entity per game tick), and not filtered. Player-only filters (naked/friends/teammates/bots) fold away when Players isn't a selected type
targeting.friends: a case-insensitive name set persisted to friends.json; Friends.is(name) gates radar colours, name tags and the Ignore Friends filter; toggled with a chat command
targeting.teammate_detection: never attack your own team: isTeammate = same vanilla scoreboard team, OR same non-white name colour as you (team colour, else the first colour in the display name; -1 when white/none so two white names don't match). Uses the entity's own team/display-name colour, NOT getTeamColor() (ESP outline overrides that)
targeting.anti_bot_filter: the Ignore Bots filter reads AntiBotModule.isBot(e), a per-tick cached behaviour-score verdict (see modules.AntiBot), so aura/clicker/visuals all skip flagged fake players through the same gate
targeting.dev_hook: a dev system property makes armor stands count as Players, to test player-only visuals/aim on a summoned dummy

packet_engine.about: One service holds packets on the client's own connection and releases them in order; backs BackTrack, FakeLag, Blink, KnockbackDelay and Velocity-delay. Incoming decided on the Netty thread, released on the main thread through vanilla's own dispatch; outgoing queued from any thread and re-sent from the main thread.
packet_engine.queues: Concurrent ordered queues carry packet, monotonic sequence, originating connection/session/world generation, release deadline and callback/flush metadata. A clear must invalidate in-flight stale producers, not only empty existing entries.
packet_engine.rules: Owner-aware slots distinguish hold, ordered pass, flush-before-pass and semantically safe immediate controls. Returning zero does not exempt a packet from an existing head-of-line hold.
packet_engine.conflict_resolution: PacketConflicts: before claiming a slot, if another ENABLED module holds it, switch that one off with a toast ('FakeLag turned off Blink - both use outgoing packet timing') instead of silently overwriting and leaving the loser enabled-but-dead
packet_engine.reentrancy: Use a one-use exact receiver+packet replay token and restore previous thread-local state in finally; a broad boolean can exempt unrelated nested sends. Incoming replay uses the proper dispatch thread and validates connection/world generation as well as listener acceptance.
packet_engine.allowlist: Ordinary movement delay keeps required version-specific tick-end markers with movement; otherwise a live marker may flush the backlog each tick. Actions, container/prediction state and control packets need explicit ordering and effective keepalive/teleport/configuration handling.
packet_engine.ordering: Merge dependencies and capture release cutoffs by monotonic arrival sequence, not wall-clock milliseconds. Respawn may replace a world while retaining a listener; drain old-state entries before its barrier or discard them according to semantics.
packet_engine.flush_pause: Apply explicit correction/attack/hurt lifecycle policy; bind replay to its originating connection. Count attempted, queued, dispatched and dropped events separately, with documented callback completion on discard.
packet_engine.hazards_avoided: holding keep-alive -> kick; holding block/use -> inventory/block desync + rejected actions; holding past a setback -> acting on a stale position (setback detector); speeding the clock instead of delaying -> timer flag; touching the integrated server's connection -> guard every entry on 'is this the client's own play-state game connection'

placement.shared_service: Carry one immutable candidate {target,support,face,hitPoint} through planning and execution. Validate replaceability, actual reach, occlusion, held item, ownership and alignment policy before acting. consumesAction may mean opening an interactive support, not placing a block; distinguish attempted/predicted/confirmed placement.
placement.hit_vec_jitter: If varying a face point, sample once inside its real geometry and reuse the same point for planning, alignment, raytrace and action. Do not pre-aim at a center then click a freshly jittered point.
placement.shared_planner: A shared frontier may rank currently reachable valid candidates by rotation cost. A bounded multistep planner must model hypothetical supports and collision/visibility dependencies rather than assume every expanded cell is already solid or use a hard-coded reach. Revalidate each step against the live world.
scaffold_specifics: half-block-aware placeY: feet at .5 on a slab -> build from floor(y), else floor(y)-1
nearest-first ring of feet spots (next-tick landing, diagonal corner-fills, current column)
Expand re-anchor: reach the 8 neighbouring columns if the feet column can't be filled
Legit predictive edge-sneak on a randomized human hold; GodBridge/TellyBridge place under feet while walking/airborne, never above start-Y+Y-increase
clutch_specifics: Scan reachable visible supports around the predicted landing path.
Gate rotate-first action on the selected actual/sent rotation; an aim callback after use cannot validate that earlier action.
Measure alignment timeout from the current attempt, not an uninitialized or previous-success timestamp that makes the first attempt an immediate emergency.
Use owner/session slot restoration and bounded idempotent release after landing, cancellation or loss of prerequisites.

damage_model.explosion: normalise distance by radius*2 (power6 crystal -> 12); impact=(1-d)*exposure; raw=((imp^2+imp)/2*7*q+1); reduce by armour+toughness, blast/generic protection (blast counts double), Resistance
damage_model.exposure: fire a small grid of rays from across the target hitbox back to the blast centre; fraction unobstructed = seen-percent (also used as placement efficiency)
damage_model.reachability: Raytrace to the actual candidate face using current reach and replaceability. Treat a full-sturdy-face filter as a conservative policy, not a universal requirement; distinguish consumed interaction from confirmed placement.

techniques.item_score: shared comparator driven off the item's own attribute modifiers (robust across versions): armour = armour pts + toughness/2 (+protection); weapon = attack damage + per-enchant bonuses; tool = dig speed + efficiency/fortune. Feeds auto-armor best-per-slot + 2-set swap, auto-weapon, and a better-than-equipped loot gate
techniques.anti_bot: Combine independent received entity/profile/team evidence with scoped identity, expiry and confidence. Hovering/unlisted/rank cues may have legitimate causes; avoid treating one cue or a fixed score as conclusive.
techniques.esp_render: A world-space box overlay pattern is available (ESP 'World' mode) alongside the screen-projected modes. World mode (WorldMesh + WorldRenderTypes) builds camera-RELATIVE line + fill geometry on the CPU and submits it inside the level render pass via collector.submitCustomGeometry, so it depth-tests and occludes against terrain like real world geometry (no bobbing/FOV drift, no behind-camera flicker). Mechanics: (1) each box = 12 edge polylines + optional 6 filled faces at ~14% of the edge alpha; (2) lines are expanded to camera-facing ribbon QUADS on the CPU: side dir = normalize(tangent x eyeRay), half-width in world units = (halfPx+1px)*worldPerPx*depth so the on-screen width is depth-independent, with a 1px anti-aliased feather carried in UV0.x (signed px from the line centre) and the core half-width in a per-vertex LineWidth attribute; (3) near-plane clip at depth 0.1 along the forward vector: an edge with one endpoint behind the camera is TRIMMED to the near plane (lerp pos+colour), not dropped — this is the fix for the screen-projection flicker; (4) a VISIBLE/HIDDEN render-type pair partitions the screen by depth (reversed-Z: visible=GEQUAL, hidden=LESS), the hidden through-wall pass drawn first at ~0.28 alpha; both share a small depth bias so faces lying on a block don't z-fight. worldPerPx is derived from 2/(framebufferHeight*projMatrix.m11). For a 2D fallback: it now keeps only the in-front corners and shrinks the box to the visible part (min/max of non-behind corners) instead of returning the moment one corner crosses behind the camera. A shared world projector still captures the exact modelview (camera*bob*shake) and projection (dynamic FOV) for the screen-projected modes; chams draw targets through walls (depth off) and must be exempt from culling; a framebuffer edge-detect pass gives a clean silhouette outline

rules: Transactional enable with rollback and bounded consecutive tick-error handling.
Cancel deferred clicks, chat and item sequences on disable/re-enable/session replacement.
Owner/session hotbar leases respect manual slot changes; shared option overrides use one baseline.
Bind plans to screen/menu/player/world; validate source/destination/cursor per actual click.
Use merchant-state observations, bounded transfer budgets and explicit pickup/place when QUICK_MOVE is rejected.
Trash only explicitly scoped spare items; reacquire reachable water from current position after sale.
Reject focused text entry for inventory movement; keep background automation focus exceptions owner-specific.
Combine received profiles, loaded entities, team metadata and genuinely attributed recent chat.
Normalize rank words; handle UUID/name identity, ignore precedence, weak-evidence expiry and alert debounce.
Unlisted/team-only/departed evidence is uncertain; it must not imply universal vanish detection or automatic disconnect.
Verify final consumed input, effects, momentum, player-width collision, supported transitions and no-progress recovery for any ground, water, climbing, glide or authorized-flight route.
Authorized-flight entry and continuation differ: bounded sprint press, vanilla acknowledgement, retained forward latch and actual boosted collision checks.
Prevent bot ascent pulses from toggling manual double-jump flight; preserve manual behavior outside ownership.
Stable interior enclosure survey, fixture-aware work, whole-layer confirmation and collision-safe outside recovery.
Long passes, reachable forward faces and tangent-continuous handoffs reduce unnecessary stop/start transitions.
Separate local break completions from attempts and server-confirmed results; deduplicate bounded callbacks.
Normalize scoreboard labels/prefix/suffix/suffix magnitudes with decimal balances and fresh post-gap baselines.
Report net rates over observed time with warmup/missing-data states; distinguish session, rolling and peak windows.
Observe the incoming server announcement path on the game thread; separate server/player/local provenance and test captured text.
Readiness availability may survive menus or other tasks; an active effect has its own activation-based deadline.
Expose detected, deferred, attempted, confirmed and failed states; do not replay past chat on enable.
Cancel on player/world/connection replacement and never repeat a consumed activation after interruption.
Record only deliberate manual commands/inputs into bounded named steps/waits; never record playback as new manual input.
One paced playback owner, no stall catch-up, current destination/session checks and cancellation on panic/context replacement.

patterns.name: Shared A* placement planner (PlacementSearch)
patterns.summary: Share immutable placement candidates and currently placeable frontiers across callers. For multistep A*, model hypothetical placed supports, actual interaction reach and visibility, and revalidate each action. A consumed interaction is not proof a block was placed; planner availability is not proof every caller enforces alignment.

patterns.name: Opportunistic backtrack rewind
patterns.summary: Hold a target's movement packets only while the delayed position sits FURTHER ALONG YOUR AIM RAY than the live one (and the ghost stays reachable + in front of the crosshair); flush the moment it isn't, you take knockback, or they stop backing off. Buys reach without piling on flaggable desync out of its window.

patterns.name: Legal hitbox expansion
patterns.summary: Widen a hitbox to aim more easily, but project the outgoing interaction vector back onto the REAL box edge so the attack packet the server receives still lands on the genuine hitbox — the expansion helps you, the server sees a legal hit.

patterns.name: Range-gated exploits
patterns.summary: Engage fakelag/timer/kb-delay only when an enemy is within N blocks and roughly ahead, via a shared nearest-enemy-within(range,angle) predicate, so you're never conspicuously desynced out of combat. Dynamic fakelag lags while closing then dumps the backlog at reach; Repel lags only while your velocity points at the target.

patterns.name: True 3D world-space ESP (ribbon lines in the level pass)
patterns.summary: Emit camera-relative line+fill geometry inside the level render pass so boxes depth-test and occlude like world geometry (survive bobbing/FOV). Lines are expanded on the CPU into camera-facing ribbon quads with depth-independent width (halfPx*worldPerPx*depth), a 1px edge-UV feather and a per-vertex LineWidth; edges crossing behind the camera are trimmed to a near plane (depth 0.1), not dropped, which kills the screen-projection flicker. Draw a visible pass (depth GEQUAL) and a faded hidden through-wall pass (depth LESS) with a shared depth bias; fills at ~14% alpha. Screen-projected corner lines remain the simpler 2D-overlay alternative (and were fixed to shrink to the in-front corners rather than vanish when one corner goes behind you). Pair with a framebuffer edge-detect outline for a clean silhouette.

patterns.name: Log-normal rotation/timing realism
patterns.summary: Sample per-tick turn speeds and click intervals from a right-skewed log-normal exp(N(0,sigma)) (median 1, e.g. HumanAim pace = clamp(exp(N(0,0.14)),0.72,1.6)) rather than a symmetric uniform band or a symmetric gaussian — both are tells, real human turn speeds are right-skewed. Layer drifting multi-sine jitter oscillators and per-target randomized gains so no signal is a clean metronome.

patterns.name: Shared control claims
patterns.summary: Use distinct owner/priority/session claims for rotation, movement, primary attack, secondary use, hotbar selections and packet slots. Refused claims block dependent actions; owner-checked release and session validation prevent stale cancellation/restoration. Shared graphics overrides use one baseline and preserve user edits.

threat_model.about: Detector-family strategies and validation boundaries; detailed procedures live in the single anticheat reference. Product names and arbitrary numeric thresholds do not establish the active server checks.

detector_families.movement_prediction: Compare actual final input and authoritative abilities/effects/impulses with version-specific collision/integration; client-only edits can disagree.
detector_families.rotation: Validate every final contributor, elapsed-time behavior, quantization contract and real action ray. Noise is not acceptance evidence.
detector_families.timing_cps_order: Revalidate every actual click, cooldown, monotonic deadline and action order; scheduled/queued/dispatched counters are distinct.
detector_families.reach_hitbox: Use current authorized range and the actual eye ray against real geometry, not only an assisted selection volume.
detector_families.block_interaction: Support, hit point, direction, break/use state and acknowledgement must agree with the current world.
detector_families.knockback_response: A reduced or jittered server impulse can still diverge from the authoritative trajectory.
detector_families.setback_rubberband: Accept corrections/acknowledgements and invalidate stale work; a correction alone does not identify a check.
detector_families.protocol_order_latency: Preserve control barriers, tick batches and original session ordering; measure real RTT rather than assume a universal lag allowance.

detector_to_counter.counter: Use final normalized input, server-authorized state and full-body braking/collision traces.
Validate final output and actual sent rays across target/owner/FPS transitions.
Share a current-prerequisite gate across primary, assist and delayed clicks.
Retain a real candidate and revalidate live geometry and observed completion.
Use generation-bound queues, sequence cutoffs, effective control handling and correction barriers.

threat_model.rule_of_thumb: Fix state/protocol inconsistencies before tuning distributions. Record source, simulation, hook and actual server evidence separately; acceptance remains unverified without a matching observed run.

modules.summary: Smoothly pulls the real camera toward a target, per frame.

modules.name: AutoClicker
modules.summary: Automated clicking at a target CPS, plus a mace-smash triggerbot.
modules.technique: Per-frame scheduler. Normal (random/drifting CPS), Humanized (click styles + fatigue/bursts + range-aware + misclicks), Click Assist (amplifies each real click), Triggerbot (clicks the crosshair entity when the swing charges; Mace Smash fires only on a qualifying fall-smash, with optional Stun-Slam axe-then-mace). Optional Charge Gate (Normal/Humanized): hold each scheduled click until getAttackStrengthScale(0f) >= a per-click randomized target gateTarget = 0.88 + rand*0.12 (i.e. [0.88,1.0], capped at 1.0), retrying each frame and re-rolling the target after each click — so you never click through the attack cooldown for a 0-knockback reset hit; more damage per swing and the cadence matches the weapon. Triggerbot uses the same idea: one click each time the scale reaches a random point in the Charge range.
modules.anticheat_notes: Lognormal gaps, OU CPS walk, repeat-gap rhythm, injected pauses, modelled press/hold, misclicks; stands down while an aura drives attacks; skips bot entities; Click Assist never free-runs; Charge Gate keeps hits on the cooldown grid. modules.name: Triggerbot
modules.summary: Attacks the entity under the crosshair once the swing is charged.
